247198067.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ovoid lymphoid tissue mass occupying the tonsillar fossa on the lateral wall of the oropharynx, bounded anteriorly by the palatoglossal arch and posteriorly by the palatopharyngeal arch.
247198067.keyConcept: Palatine Tonsil (in tonsillar fossa): Primary lymphoid organ in the tonsillar fossa of the oropharynx, supplied by the tonsillar branch of the facial artery.

1822533329.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small rounded anterior bony bar of the first cervical vertebra (atlas, C1) positioned directly in front of the odontoid process (dens of axis).
1822533329.keyConcept: Anterior arch of atlas: Anterior segment of the ring of C1 lacking a vertebral body, articulating posteriorly with the dens of axis.

1325303371.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent vertical tooth-like projection (odontoid process) arising superiorly from the body of the second cervical vertebra (axis, C2), situated immediately posterior to the anterior arch of atlas.
1325303371.keyConcept: Dense of axis: Odontoid process of C2 acting as the pivot for rotational head movement at the atlantoaxial joint.

1865261173.explanation: Criteria of Identification: First typical cervical vertebral body situated immediately inferior to the axis (C2), separated from it by the C2-C3 intervertebral disc.
1865261173.keyConcept: 3rd Cervical vertebra: Typical cervical vertebra positioned directly below C2 (axis).

361615538.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Muscular excretory duct arising from the anterior border of the parotid gland, crossing horizontally over the masseter muscle before piercing the buccinator.
361615538.keyConcept: Parotid duct (Stensen's duct): Traverses the masseter, pierces the buccinator, and opens into the oral cavity opposite the maxillary second molar.

2013444071.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Long excretory duct emerging from the deep lobe of the submandibular gland, coursing forward along the floor of the mouth medial to the sublingual gland.
2013444071.keyConcept: Submandibular duct (Wharton's duct): Courses between mylohyoid and hyoglossus muscles, crossed by the lingual nerve, to open at the sublingual caruncle.

133957652.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Row of multiple tiny excretory duct orifices and conduits emerging from the sublingual gland along the crest of the sublingual fold.
133957652.keyConcept: Sublingual ducts (ducts of Rivinus): 8–20 small excretory ducts that drain the sublingual gland directly into the oral cavity along the plica sublingualis.

2075756875.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Smallest of the major salivary glands, situated submucosally in the floor of the mouth within the sublingual fossa of the mandible superior to the mylohyoid muscle.
2075756875.keyConcept: Sublingual gland: Predominantly mucous-secreting salivary gland in the sublingual fossa of the mandible, innervated by CN VII via the chorda tympani.

1932998699.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large lobulated salivary gland located anteroinferior to the ear, occupying the retromandibular space superficial to the masseter and sternocleidomastoid muscles.
1932998699.keyConcept: Parotid gland: Largest salivary gland; purely serous, enveloped by investing deep cervical fascia, and traversed by the facial nerve (CN VII).

6120767.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Paired salivary gland located in the submandibular (digastric) triangle of the neck, wrapping around the posterior free border of the mylohyoid muscle.
6120767.keyConcept: Submandibular gland: Mixed seromucous gland in the digastric triangle responsible for the majority of baseline unstimulated saliva production.

2001654882.explanation: Criteria of Identification: V-shaped shallow groove on the dorsum of the tongue running anterolaterally from the foramen caecum, separating the anterior two-thirds from the posterior one-third.
2001654882.keyConcept: Sulcus terminalis: V-shaped landmark dividing the anterior oral tongue (presulcal, arch 1) from the posterior pharyngeal tongue (postsulcal, arches 3/4).

859364234.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small blind pit located at the median apex of the V-shaped sulcus terminalis on the dorsal surface of the tongue.
859364234.keyConcept: Foramen caecum: Nonfunctional midline pit at the sulcus terminalis apex marking the site of origin and descent of the embryonic thyroglossal duct.

345759851.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Compact oval mass of lymphoid tissue situated laterally in the tonsillar sinus between the diverging palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.
345759851.keyConcept: Palatine tonsils: Paired lymphoid aggregates situated between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches; key components of Waldeyer's lymphatic ring.

1737597847.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Aggregations of lymphoid nodules creating a cobblestone, irregular surface texture on the posterior one-third (pharyngeal surface) of the tongue behind the sulcus terminalis.
1737597847.keyConcept: Lingual tonsils: Lymphoid nodules on the posterior third of the tongue innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX); lack true crypts.

1990317627.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Thin, flexible leaf-like fibrocartilaginous structure situated posterior to the base of the tongue, forming the anterior boundary of the laryngeal inlet.
1990317627.keyConcept: Epiglottis: Elastic fibrocartilage projecting behind the tongue base that folds over the laryngeal inlet to protect the airway during swallowing.

1691415355.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Anterior vertical mucosal fold extending inferiorly and laterally from the soft palate to the lateral border of the tongue, overlying the palatoglossus muscle.
1691415355.keyConcept: Palatoglossal arch (anterior pillar of fauces): Demarcates the boundary of the oropharyngeal isthmus; contains palatoglossus muscle innervated by CN X.

432149818.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elevated paired ridge of mucous membrane running anteromedially in the floor of the mouth on either side of the frenulum, produced by the underlying sublingual gland.
432149818.keyConcept: Sublingual fold (plica sublingualis): Mucosal elevation overlying the sublingual gland that bears the openings of the minor sublingual ducts.

2130874993.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Midline vertical sagittal fold of mucous membrane connecting the undersurface of the tongue to the floor of the mouth.
2130874993.keyConcept: Lingual frenulum: Midline fold tethering the ventral tongue; congenitally short frenulum causes ankyloglossia (tongue-tie).

2083777564.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Smooth, thin, non-keratinized mucosal underside (ventral surface) of the tongue, visible when elevated, revealing the midline lingual frenulum and deep lingual veins.
2083777564.keyConcept: Inferior surface of tongue: Non-papillated ventral tongue mucosa with visible deep lingual veins; ideal site for sublingual drug administration.

1952003934.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Four-way cruciate suture intersection on the oral surface of the hard palate formed by the perpendicular crossing of the median palatine suture and transverse palatine suture.
1952003934.keyConcept: Cruciform suture: Cross-shaped junction between the median palatine and transverse palatine sutures uniting the maxillae and palatine bones.
